opening_message:
Ticket 1: Matthew Mejia (employee ID E034) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E034.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Employee is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Payroll. As full-time employee, max is write (admin reserved for the owning role, Payroll Specialist). Requested level matches max, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record shows E034 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max at read (write requires advanced training; admin never allowed). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The HR and Security records conflict on the employee's status: HR states E034 is a full-time Analyst (max write for Payroll), while Security states E034 is a contractor with basic training (max read for Payroll; write requires advanced training). Given the conflicting evidence, grant the level that is safe and compliant under both records. Read is at or below the maximum in both interpretations and never exceeds the requested write level, whereas write would violate policy if the Security record (contractor, basic training) is correct. Grant read.
